stations.title: The first monks
stations.text: Benedictine monks from Calabria in southern Italy settled here and began to build a church and monastery. After about forty years they left the place again, before canons regular completed the building.

stations.title: Cistercians from Champagne
stations.text: A group of Cistercian monks from Trois-Fontaines Abbey in Champagne arrived in Orval in 1132 and merged with the existing community under the first abbot, Constantin.

stations.title: Devastated in the Thirty Years’ War
stations.text: In 1637 French mercenary troops plundered and burned the abbey during the Thirty Years’ War.

stations.title: Burned down in the Revolution
stations.text: In 1793 French revolutionary troops burned the abbey to the ground—in retaliation for having given shelter to Austrian troops. The community was forcibly dispersed.

stations.title: The ruins are returned
stations.text: For over a century Orval remained a ruin, until the Harenne family donated the land to the Cistercian Order in 1926 so that monastic life could be possible there again.

stations.title: Beer for the rebuilding
stations.text: The new abbey was built from 1926 under the Trappist Marie-Albert van der Cruyssen. In 1931 the monks revived the medieval art of brewing—not out of tradition, but to finance the rebuilding.

stations.title: The new church
stations.text: With the consecration of the new abbey church on September 8, 1948, the rebuilding was essentially complete. To this day Orval brews only this one beer.
